overall_diagnosis: Across all samples, the failure is attributed to omissions and inconsistencies in maven-build-lifecycle/SKILL.md. The skill file’s “build-repair artifact contract” is incomplete/misaligned with benchmark expectations (broken numbering; unclear/overly hardcoded paths; missing explicit requirement to write the diagnosis artifact and to create/apply a real patch). The “minimal diagnostic sequence” is also insufficient (only a cd), lacking canonical Maven reproduction commands and guidance for multi-module selection. Finally, it lacks clear instructions for choosing the correct Maven/JDK toolchain (mvnw vs system Maven, toolchains, compiler release/source/target) and for dealing with nested/invoker-style integration test projects (e.g., src/it) where dependency resolution and acceptable modification scope differ (reactor install, which POM to edit, avoiding generated fixtures).

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The build-repair contract and diagnostic workflow are incomplete and internally inconsistent: the checklist numbering starts at 2; the contract is hardcoded to a specific repo path and does not clearly generalize to /home/travis/build/failed/<org>/<repo>; it does not explicitly require writing the diagnosis artifact to /home/travis/build/failed/failed_reasons.txt; and it does not clearly require creating a non-empty unified diff at the task-specific patch path and applying it (verifying actual repo file changes). The minimal diagnostic sequence provides only `cd` and lacks a standard set of Maven commands/flags to reproduce failures in legacy multi-module builds. Additionally, the skill lacks explicit toolchain selection guidance (mvnw vs mvn; Java version/toolchains; reading .mvn/jvm.config and compiler plugin settings) and dedicated guidance for nested/invoker integration test projects (e.g., src/it): how to locate them, how dependency resolution works (reactor vs local repo), and what modification scope is appropriate (root/parent POM vs nested test POM vs generated artifacts).
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Revise maven-build-lifecycle/SKILL.md as follows: (1) Fix and expand the “Build-repair artifact contract”: correct list numbering; explicitly require creating /home/travis/build/failed/failed_reasons.txt; generalize repo path patterns to /home/travis/build/failed/<org>/<repo>; require creating at least one non-empty unified diff at /home/travis/build/failed/<org>/<repo>/patch_1.diff (and/or patch_{i}.diff) and explicitly require applying the patch and verifying real project file changes via git diff/status. Avoid hardcoding google/auto in the contract text. (2) Replace/extend “Minimal diagnostic sequence” with an ordered, canonical reproduction workflow: check versions (`java -version`, `mvn -version`), prefer `./mvnw` if present, run `mvn -e` (optionally `-X`) with typical phases (`clean test` / `verify`), include toggles like `-DskipTests` for bisecting, and document multi-module targeting via `-pl`/`-am`. (3) Add a “Toolchain selection” subsection: read `.mvn/jvm.config`, `maven-compiler-plugin` release/source/target, and toolchains.xml if present; prefer aligning with project-required JDK rather than ad-hoc JAVA_HOME changes; note how mismatched JDKs cause non-reproducible CI results. (4) Add a dedicated “Nested/Invoker integration test projects (src/it)” subsection: how to find nested POMs; when invoker runs require `mvn install` to seed the local repo; guidance on invoker-related flags if applicable; and a clear scope rule—prefer fixing root/module POMs and build config; only edit nested test project POMs when those fixtures are source-controlled and intentionally require adjustment; never edit generated `target/` outputs or local repository artifacts.
